threads.thread_goal: Align on MVP scope and system requirements across all roles.

messages.text:
Kicking off the connected monitoring module work for project_title: Launch of Connected Industrial Monitoring Module.
I have a first draft of the MVP requirements in A1, mapped to T1. The proposal is to focus the first 30 days on:
- Monitoring vibration and temperature on 2–3 critical assets per line
- Basic alerting to existing PLC/SCADA via digital outputs
- Edge buffering for short connectivity drops
- Simple dashboard and CSV export for the pilot only

Before we freeze this, I need input from each of you on:
- Any must-have signals or interfaces for the first pilot
- Constraints that might affect enclosure, wiring, or manufacturability

Please skim A1 today and drop comments here so we can converge on the MVP scope and the minimal data set for the pilot.

I went through A1 quickly. From a mechanical side, I see mounting and IP requirements are still marked as assumptions.
For T2 I need to know:
- Whether we commit to panel mounting only for the MVP
- Target IP rating for the enclosure in the pilot plants

Without that, I might overdesign and hurt cost. Can we capture these in A1 before we call the MVP frozen?

From the electrical side, A1 looks reasonable for a first pass.
For T3, I suggest we keep the MVP to:
- 2 analog inputs (for vibration and temperature) plus 1 spare
- 2 digital outputs for alarms to PLC
- Single 24 VDC supply, no mains inside the box

This keeps the safety checklist in A2 simpler later. For interfaces, I would avoid adding fieldbus in the first pilot and rely on digital I/O only. Does that fit with the integration expectations?

On the data side, I aligned A1 with the draft in A4 for T4.
For the MVP pilot I propose the minimal data set to be:
- Timestamp, asset id, sensor type, value, unit
- Alarm state and reason code

Interfaces:
- Edge publishes to our backend over MQTT
- Optional CSV export locally for the plant team

For PLC/SCADA, I agree with 219209 that we keep it to digital outputs for now. That lets us validate value without getting stuck in protocol mapping. We can extend to Modbus or OPC UA later.
Any objections to this as the minimal data set for the first pilot?

Looking at A1 from a build and cost angle, and cross-checking with what we will need for T6 and T8.
If we keep the MVP to 2–3 assets per line and the I/O set that 219209 suggested, I think we can stay within the cost ceiling, but I need to confirm once we have a first BOM in A3.
One concern: do we need local display or buttons in the MVP? That would add parts and assembly time. If we can rely on PLC alarms and the dashboard only, it will simplify T6 and T8.

On mounting and IP for the MVP:
- Mounting: panel mounting only for the first pilot, no pole or wall brackets yet
- IP: target IP54 for now, based on the pilot lines we discussed with sales

I will update A1 accordingly under T1 so T2 has a clear reference.
If we later find a pilot that needs higher protection, we can treat that as a follow-on iteration, not part of the frozen MVP.

The proposed I/O set works for the pilot customers we have in mind.
For the MVP, let us lock in:
- 2 analog inputs plus 1 spare
- 2 digital outputs for alarms
- 24 VDC supply only

I will reflect this in A1 so that T3 and T4 are aligned. For the pilot, we will validate that digital alarms are enough to trigger their existing workflows.

Thanks, that helps.
With panel mounting and IP54 confirmed for the MVP, I can keep the enclosure concept simple for T2 and avoid extra seals and brackets.
I will still leave some space margin inside for wiring flexibility, but I will not design for outdoor exposure in this first round.

To close the loop on the minimal data set and interfaces for the pilot:
- Data fields: timestamp, asset id, sensor type, value, unit, alarm state, reason code
- Interfaces: MQTT to backend plus local CSV export; PLC integration via digital outputs only

I will finalize A4 with this scope for T4 and T5.
Unless someone sees a blocker, I suggest we treat this as the agreed minimal data set and interfaces for the first pilot.
No objections from my side. Keeping the PLC link to digital outputs only is consistent with the wiring plan I have in mind for T3 and keeps the safety review with A2 manageable in the time we have.

On the local display question: from a build and cost standpoint, I recommend we skip it for the MVP.
If we rely on PLC alarms and the backend dashboard, we avoid extra components and assembly steps, which will help T6 and T8 stay within the time and cost targets.
If everyone agrees, we should mark local display as out of scope in A1.

Aligned. For the MVP:
- No local display or buttons
- Operators will see alarms via PLC/SCADA and the pilot dashboard

I will mark local HMI as explicitly out of scope in A1 under T1.
With that, I think we have a consistent MVP feature list that fits the 30-day window and the pilot constraints.

From the software side, the current MVP scope in A1 and A4 is implementable within the 30 days for a pilot-ready prototype, assuming we keep edge logic to basic acquisition, buffering, and alarm evaluation for T5.
I will avoid adding analytics or predictive models in this first round and treat those as future enhancements.

Given the clarified scope in A1, I am comfortable that T3 can be completed in time and that we can pass the initial safety checks in A2 before we commit to any PCB or enclosure details.
I will flag if I see any late surprises once we start selecting specific components.

With the MVP scope now clearer in A1, I will adjust my T2 plan to focus on a compact panel-mount enclosure with enough space for the I/O and wiring that 219209 outlined.
I will not plan for extra cutouts or external controls in this first design.

From a manufacturing and cost perspective, the current MVP in A1 looks workable.
I will start a rough cost view in A3 under T8 based on the I/O and enclosure assumptions we just aligned on, and I will sketch a simple pilot build flow for T6.
If the first pass shows any cost pressure, I will bring options back here before we change scope.

Summarizing where we landed so we can move forward:
- MVP features: 2–3 assets per line, vibration and temperature monitoring, digital alarm outputs to PLC, edge buffering, pilot dashboard and CSV export, no local display
- Hardware constraints: panel mounting, IP54, 24 VDC supply, 2 analog inputs plus 1 spare, 2 digital outputs
- Data and interfaces: minimal data set and MQTT plus CSV as described in A4, PLC via digital outputs only

Unless there are last-minute objections today, I will mark A1 as approved for the MVP and treat the feature list as frozen for this first pilot.
No further comments from me. With D1 and D2 in place, I will proceed to finalize A4 and start the edge prototype work under T5 according to the agreed MVP scope.

threads.thread_goal: Converge on hardware, enclosure, and electrical design choices.

messages.text:
I have a first pass of the mechanical and enclosure design for the monitoring module based on the MVP scope in A1 and the mounting/IP assumptions we aligned on.
For T2, I drafted a compact panel-mount enclosure with IP54 sealing and enough space for the I/O and wiring that 219209 proposed for T3.
Key open points where I need feedback from electrical and production:
- Terminal block layout: is the current arrangement practical for wiring and safety per A2?
- Internal clearances: do we have enough room for cable routing and strain relief?
- Any manufacturability concerns for T6 or cost flags for T8?
I can share the CAD views in our usual folder; let us use this thread to converge on the enclosure concept and confirm mounting and IP requirements.

I reviewed your CAD screenshots.
From an electrical standpoint for T3 and A2:
- Terminal blocks: spacing looks tight near the corners. For safer wiring and to meet creepage/clearance guidance in A2, I recommend shifting the power terminals away from the signal terminals by at least one pitch.
- Grounding: I do not see a clear provision for a grounding stud or bar. We should add a dedicated grounding point tied to the enclosure.
- Cable entry: two cable glands may not be enough if we have separate sensor bundles and power. I suggest planning for at least three entries.
If we adjust these, I will be more comfortable signing off that the schematics and wiring can meet the safety checklist later.

From a build and cost angle for T6 and T8:
- The current enclosure size is ok for manual assembly, but the number of different fasteners looks high. If we can standardize on fewer screw types, it will simplify work instructions and reduce risk of errors.
- The cable gland positions are fine for now, but if we add a third as 219209 suggests, let us keep them aligned to make drilling or punching easier.
- The internal DIN rail length seems longer than needed. Shortening it slightly could save a bit of cost and free space for cable loops.
No blocking issues, but these tweaks would help manufacturability and cost in A3.

Thanks for the detailed feedback.
I can adjust the layout in T2 to:
- Separate power and signal terminals by one pitch and add a small barrier between them
- Add a grounding stud on the backplate tied to the enclosure
- Increase the number of cable glands from two to three and align them for easier machining
I will update the CAD and share new views so you can re-check against A2.

Those changes sound good.
On my side, for T3 I will keep the schematics aligned with your updated layout:
- Separate terminal blocks for power and signals
- Clear grounding symbol and connection to the stud you add
- Labeling that matches the physical positions to reduce wiring mistakes
Once your updated T2 is ready, I will run a quick pass against A2 to confirm we are not missing any obvious safety gaps.

On the fasteners and DIN rail:
If you can standardize on one screw size for the enclosure and internal mounting in T2, it will simplify the assembly steps I am drafting for T6.
For T8, I will assume the updated enclosure and hardware when I refresh A3. If the cost per unit starts to creep up, we might need to look at alternative enclosure suppliers, but I would prefer to keep the concept stable for this pilot.

Understood. I will revise T2 to use a single screw type where possible and trim the DIN rail length.
I will also double-check that the panel cutout and mounting holes remain compatible with the panel-mount approach we agreed in A1.
Once I have the updated drawings, I will share a short note here so we can confirm the enclosure concept.

Switching to the electrical schematics status for T3:
I have a draft that matches the MVP I/O set from A1:
- 2 analog inputs plus 1 spare
- 2 digital outputs
- 24 VDC supply with fuse and reverse polarity protection

I ran it against the main items in A2 and did not see critical gaps, but I want to validate:
- Do we need any additional surge protection for the pilot environments?
- Are we ok to keep the analog inputs non-isolated for this first run, given the limited scope?
If we agree on these points, I can mark the schematics as ready for prototype build once your enclosure updates are in place.

On surge protection and isolation for the pilot:
- The two pilot plants we are targeting have relatively clean 24 VDC control power, and they already use similar sensor wiring. For the MVP, I think basic surge protection on the supply is enough.
- For analog inputs, non-isolated is acceptable for this first pilot as long as we clearly document wiring limits and grounding in A1 and the playbook later.
If we see noise or grounding issues during T7 lab tests, we can plan an isolated input variant for the next iteration.

From a build and cost perspective, adding full isolation on the analog inputs now would likely push us over the target in A3 for T8.
Given what 81818 said about the pilot sites, I support keeping the inputs non-isolated for this first run and revisiting after we see real data from T7 and the pilot.
I will note this as an assumption in my manufacturability notes for T6.

I have updated the enclosure design in T2 with:
- Three aligned cable glands
- Separate power and signal terminal areas
- Grounding stud on the backplate
- Standardized screw type and shorter DIN rail

Mounting and IP54 are unchanged from A1.
Unless you see any major issues, I suggest we treat this as the baseline enclosure concept for the pilot.

I checked your updated layout against my T3 draft and the A2 checklist.
With the separated terminals, grounding stud, and extra cable gland, I do not see any blocking safety issues for the pilot.
On the schematics side, with the agreed non-isolated inputs and basic surge protection, I am comfortable saying the design is ready for prototype build, as long as we keep an eye on wiring practices during assembly.

From my side, the updated enclosure concept in T2 is workable for T6, and the electrical design you described for T3 fits our assembly capabilities.
I will proceed to draft the pilot build process and update A3 with the latest enclosure and component assumptions for T8.
Let us treat the current enclosure concept and mounting/IP requirements as locked for this pilot so we do not churn the mechanical design.

threads.thread_goal: Define and validate the data architecture and edge software plan.

messages.text:
I have posted the initial data architecture and API spec in A4, aligned with the MVP scope in A1 and the decisions from D1 and D2.
For T4, the proposal is:
- Edge device collects sensor data and alarm states
- Local buffering in a small queue on the device
- MQTT to our backend with a simple JSON payload
- Optional CSV export for the pilot plants

For T5, the first edge software iteration will focus on acquisition, buffering, and basic alarm evaluation only.
I would like feedback on:
- Any additional data fields needed for T7 tests or pilot analysis
- Latency and reliability expectations from the application side
- Any constraints from production on hardware resources that might affect the edge stack

Thanks for sharing A4.
From an application and testing perspective for T7:
- The data fields you listed cover what we need for the pilot acceptance criteria and for basic downtime analysis.
- For latency, if we can keep end-to-end delay under a few seconds for alarms, that is enough for the first pilot.
- Reliability: I would like the edge buffer to handle at least a few hours of data in case of network issues, so we do not lose events during short outages.
If we can meet these, I do not see a need to add more complexity in the first iteration.

On hardware resource constraints from a build standpoint:
We have not finalized the exact controller yet, but for T6 and T8 I am assuming a modest embedded platform, not a high-end PC.
If the edge software in T5 can run with limited CPU and memory and does not require special storage beyond a small flash, that will help keep the BOM in A3 under control.
If you foresee any need for larger storage or more powerful hardware, please flag it early so we can factor it into T8.

From the electrical side, the main concern is that the data architecture in A4 stays compatible with the I/O and power scheme in T3.
As long as the edge device can operate reliably on 24 VDC and does not require additional field wiring beyond what we already planned, I do not see major constraints.
One request: please make sure the edge software exposes clear status indicators (even if only via the backend or CSV) so we can correlate any electrical issues with data gaps during T7.

On latency and buffering:
- For alarms, I will target sub-second processing on the edge and a few seconds end-to-end to the backend, assuming normal network conditions.
- For buffering, I will design T5 to store several hours of data in a local queue, with backoff and retry logic for MQTT.
I will document these targets explicitly in A4 so they are visible in the test plan for T7.

On resource usage:
The current T5 plan is to use a lightweight runtime with:
- Modest CPU needs (simple polling and threshold checks)
- A small in-memory buffer plus periodic flush to flash
- No heavy analytics or databases in the MVP
This should fit on a low to mid-range embedded controller. I will avoid dependencies that would force us into more expensive hardware, and I will note the assumed minimum specs in A4 so you can reflect them in A3 for T8.

On status indicators: for T7 and the pilot, it would help if we can see at least:
- Edge device online or offline
- Last successful publish timestamp
- Buffer fill level or a simple flag when the buffer is near full
These can be exposed in the backend UI or even in the CSV export for now. That will make it easier to separate network or power issues from software problems during troubleshooting.

Good point.
I will extend A4 and the T5 plan to include:
- Online status and last publish timestamp as part of the device metadata
- A simple buffer usage metric that we can surface in the backend and logs
This should not add much complexity but will help a lot during T7 and the pilot.

Thanks for clarifying the resource needs.
With that, I will proceed under T6 and T8 assuming we can use a cost-effective controller without extra storage modules.
If later in T5 you see that we are close to the limits, please flag it early so we can adjust the BOM in A3 before we commit to a larger pilot batch.

One more detail from the electrical side:
If the edge device logs any power-related events (for example, brownouts or restarts), it would be useful to include those in the data model in A4.
That way, during T7 and later pilots, we can correlate any anomalies with power quality without adding extra sensors.

Agreed.
I will add a simple event log structure in A4 and implement in T5:
- Power cycle events
- Configuration changes
- Communication errors
These will be low-volume but valuable for diagnostics during T7 and the pilot.

To make sure we are aligned on the minimal edge capabilities for the pilot:
- Sensor acquisition for vibration and temperature
- Local buffering for several hours
- Basic threshold-based alarm evaluation
- MQTT publish to backend plus CSV export
- Basic device and buffer status reporting
No analytics, no remote firmware updates, and no complex configuration UI in this first round.
If everyone is ok with this, we can treat it as the agreed scope for T5.

This scope for T5 works for me and fits the hardware and cost assumptions we are using in T6 and T8.
Keeping firmware updates and advanced features out of the MVP will also simplify assembly and test instructions on the shop floor.

Given the feedback so far, I propose we formally approve the data architecture and communication protocol in A4 for the MVP pilot:
- MQTT-based edge-to-cloud link
- Minimal data model we defined earlier
- Local buffering and CSV export
- Basic status and event logging
I will treat this as the baseline for T4 and T5 and avoid further changes unless we hit a critical issue in T7.

threads.thread_goal: Plan and coordinate lab tests and customer pilot installation.

messages.text:
With the MVP scope, enclosure, and data architecture now defined in A1, A2, and A4, I would like to align on the test and pilot plan.
For T7 and T11, my proposal is:
- Week 1–2: integrated lab tests following A7, focusing on functional checks, basic environmental tests, and safety checks before we go on-site
- Week 3: pilot installation at the first customer line using A5
- Week 4: pilot installation at the second line and initial data validation

I will draft detailed lab test cases in A7 and align them with the pilot acceptance criteria from T10.
Please confirm:
- Any additional tests we must include before going on-site
- Constraints on installation windows at the pilot plants
- Who will own which steps during on-site work per A5

For T10, I can draft pilot test procedures that align with your A7 plan.
From a mechanical perspective, I would like to include at least:
- Basic vibration and shock checks on the enclosure mounting
- Verification that cable routing and strain relief match the design intent
- A quick check that the panel cutout and mounting holes work as expected on the actual cabinets
I will need confirmation from the pilot sites on what kind of access we will have to their panels and how much time we can spend on mechanical checks during installation.

For lab and pilot tests from the electrical side:
In A7 and T7, I suggest we include:
- Verification of wiring against T3 schematics and A2 checklist
- Power-up and power-down sequences, including brownout simulation if possible
- Checks that digital alarm outputs behave correctly with a representative PLC input
On-site, per A5, I can own the electrical verification steps for the first pilot installation, but I will need support from the local maintenance team for panel access and lockout procedures.

From a production and pilot build standpoint for T6 and T11:
- I would like to run a small pilot build before lab tests, maybe 3–4 units, to validate the assembly process and timing.
- In A7, we should include a check that the units coming from the pilot build meet basic assembly quality criteria before they go into lab tests.
Regarding installation windows, I will coordinate with sales and the plant contacts to confirm when we can access the lines. My understanding is that we will have limited downtime windows, so we need a clear sequence in A5 to avoid overruns.

On the software side for T7 and T11:
- In A7, I will propose functional tests for data acquisition, buffering, MQTT connectivity, and CSV export.
- For the pilot, we should include a short connectivity soak test at each site to ensure the network path to the backend is stable.
I can support remotely during the on-site installations to monitor logs and data in real time, but I will not be on-site myself.

On access and timing at the pilot sites:
- For the first plant, we have a 4-hour window during a planned maintenance stop in week 3.
- For the second plant, we likely have a shorter 2-hour window in week 4.
Given that, I suggest we keep on-site mechanical checks focused on what is essential for safety and function. More detailed vibration or shock tests can be done in the lab as part of T7.
Please reflect this in T10 so the on-site steps in A5 stay realistic.

Understood.
I will structure T10 so that:
- More detailed mechanical checks happen in the lab under T7
- On-site checks in A5 are limited to verifying mounting, cable routing, and that nothing interferes with existing equipment
I will share a draft of T10 for review before we finalize the acceptance criteria.

For the on-site responsibilities in A5:
- I can own: verifying wiring, running basic electrical safety checks, and confirming PLC alarm behavior.
- 81818 can own: coordinating with the plant, validating data in the backend, and walking through the playbook with the local team.
We should document this split clearly in A5 so there is no confusion during the limited downtime windows.

I will proceed to plan the small pilot build under T6:
- Target: 4 units assembled before lab tests
- Include a short assembly quality checklist that feeds into A7
For T11, once we confirm the exact dates with the plants, I will update A5 with the agreed installation windows and any site-specific constraints, such as PPE or training requirements.

For the connectivity soak tests in A7:
- I will define a simple script under T7 that sends test messages at a fixed rate and logs any drops or retries.
- During the on-site phase of T11, we can run this for at least 30–60 minutes per site while monitoring the backend.
This should give us enough confidence in the network path without extending the installation window too much.

To make the lab test plan concrete for T7 and T10, I will structure A7 into three blocks:
- Functional: sensor readings, alarms, buffering, MQTT, CSV
- Environmental: basic temperature range and vibration checks aligned with the enclosure design
- Safety and integration: wiring checks against A2 and T3, plus PLC alarm behavior
Once we agree on this structure, I will treat A7 as the reference for go or no-go decisions before we move to T11.

The proposed A7 structure covers what I need from an electrical and safety perspective.
As long as we explicitly include a check that the units meet the A2 checklist before we ship them to the pilot sites, I am comfortable using A7 as the gate for T11.

From the mechanical side, I am fine with A7 being the main reference for lab tests.
I will make sure T10 aligns with your three-block structure so that the pilot acceptance criteria match what we validate in the lab.

Quick update on pilot site coordination for T11:
- First plant has tentatively confirmed the week 3 window; I am waiting for written confirmation of the exact day and time.
- Second plant is checking whether they can align their maintenance stop with our week 4 target.
Once I have written confirmations, I will update A5 with the specific dates and responsibilities so we can consider the pilot schedule locked.

Given the feedback, I propose we lock the lab test plan and acceptance criteria as follows:
- A7 is the single reference for lab tests under T7, structured into functional, environmental, and safety or integration blocks
- T10 defines pilot acceptance criteria that mirror A7, with any site-specific adjustments noted
- Passing A7 with no critical issues will be the condition to proceed to T11 pilot installations
If there are no objections, I will treat this as our agreed approach.
No objections from me. Using A7 as the single reference for lab tests and as the gate for T11 will also make it easier to track issues and retests.

Once we have written confirmations from both plants, I suggest we:
- Record the confirmed sites and dates in A5
- Assign named owners for each major step in the checklist (mechanical, electrical, software, customer communication)
With that in place, we can say the pilot sites, installation dates, and responsibilities are confirmed for this first rollout.

threads.thread_goal: Review pilot results and agree on next-iteration and rollout plan.

messages.text:
I have compiled a draft of the pilot feedback and next steps in A8, based on the two customer lines we installed using A5 and the test results in A7.
Key points so far:
- Technical: the modules met the MVP acceptance criteria from T10, with a few minor issues logged
- Operational: installation within the planned windows worked, but we had some delays due to panel access at the second site
- Commercial and cost: initial BOM cost in A3 is slightly above the target, but customers see enough value to continue discussions
For T12, I need your input on:
- Which technical improvements should be in the next iteration scope
- What we should adjust in the playbook A6 for broader rollout
- How we can address the cost gap highlighted in T8 without delaying the next build

From an application and customer perspective, based on A8 and the feedback we collected on-site:
- Customers appreciated the clear alarms and the simple dashboard, but they asked for a way to tag events with short comments for later analysis.
- The installation steps in A5 worked, but we should add clearer guidance on pre-checks for panel access and lockout to avoid the delays we saw at the second site.
For A6, I suggest we:
- Emphasize the value story around reduced unplanned downtime, using the early data from A8
- Add a short section on typical integration patterns with PLCs and SCADA, based on what we saw in the pilots.

Looking at the technical findings in A8 and the logs from T7 and the pilots:
- Data reliability was generally good, but we saw a few short gaps when network connectivity was unstable. The buffer handled most of them, but we should improve retry logic and add clearer alerts when the buffer is near full.
- Some users asked for more flexible alarm thresholds and schedules.
For the next iteration, I propose we prioritize in T5:
- More robust buffering and retry behavior
- Configurable alarm thresholds and basic scheduling
We can also add a simple event comment field in the backend, as 81818 mentioned, without changing the edge software too much.

From the electrical side, based on A7 and the pilot notes in A8:
- The non-isolated analog inputs worked, but we saw some noise in one of the plants with longer cable runs.
- Wiring and safety checks against A2 went smoothly, but the terminal labeling could be clearer for the local electricians.
For the next iteration, I recommend we consider in T3:
- Either adding optional isolation for analog inputs or at least improving filtering and shielding guidance in A1 and A6
- Updating terminal labels and documentation to match what electricians expect in the field.

On the mechanical side, A8 shows that the enclosure and mounting concept held up well.
The only issues I saw were:
- Tight space for cable bending in one cabinet with a lot of existing wiring
- Some confusion about which side the cable glands should face in crowded panels
For the next iteration, I can explore in T2:
- A slightly deeper enclosure option or a variant with angled cable entries
- Clearer mounting and orientation guidance in the documentation and in A6.

On the cost side, looking at A3 and T8:
- We are a bit above the target mainly due to the enclosure and some of the terminal hardware.
- The controller cost is within expectations.
To close the gap without delaying the next build, I suggest we:
- Get alternative quotes for the enclosure and terminals
- Check if we can slightly simplify the internal hardware without affecting the MVP features
I will start this work under T8 and update A3 with options and their impact on cost and lead time.

The buffering and retry improvements you propose for T5 align well with what the plant teams asked for.
For A6, I will also add a short troubleshooting section that explains how to interpret buffer-related alerts and what actions the plant should take.
On the event comments, we can start with a simple field in the backend UI and see how much it gets used before we consider more advanced workflows.

If we look for alternative terminals under T8, I will double-check that any new parts still meet the A2 safety checklist and do not complicate wiring.
I can also review whether we can simplify the wiring layout in T3 slightly without affecting functionality, which might reduce assembly time and cost.

For the deeper enclosure or angled cable entries you mentioned for T2, we should be careful not to introduce too many variants too early.
Maybe for the next build we keep a single enclosure but adjust the internal layout slightly to improve cable bending space, and we add clearer orientation diagrams in A6.
We can revisit a second enclosure variant once we have more pilots.

For the rollout plan in T12 and A6, my suggestion is:
- Next iteration scope: focus on reliability and usability improvements (buffering, alarm configuration, labeling, documentation) rather than adding new sensor types
- Rollout: expand to a small set of additional lines at the two pilot plants plus 1–2 new customers who have similar PLC and SCADA setups
This keeps the technical risk manageable while giving us more data to refine the value story.

From the software side, I support focusing the next iteration on robustness and configurability rather than new features.
For T5, I will plan the next sprint around:
- Improved buffering and retries
- Configurable thresholds and schedules
- Better logging and diagnostics to support larger rollouts
This should also make it easier to support more sites without increasing support load too much.

Summarizing for T12 based on A8 and your inputs:
- Technical focus next: reliability and usability improvements (buffering, alarm configuration, labeling, documentation), plus targeted electrical and mechanical refinements
- Cost: run T8 to close the BOM gap via alternative components and minor design simplifications, without changing the core concept
- Rollout: extend to more lines at the current pilot plants and a small number of similar new customers, using an updated A6 playbook
I will capture this in A8 as the recommended next iteration scope and rollout plan and share a short summary with leadership.
